transfers.source_mechanism: resource flow enables network adaptation under environmental constraints, producing optimized transport pathways
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: distributed network optimization through local interactions and feedback
transfers.required_translation: replace resource flow with traffic flow, network restructuring with signal timing adjustment, local sensing with loop detector measurements, and environmental constraints with traffic demand patterns
transfers.expected_effect: adaptive traffic signal timing that optimizes traffic flow through local decisions without central coordination
boundary_conditions: sensitivity to local queue length and vehicle count
failure_conditions: extreme traffic imbalance overwhelming local capacity
transfers.testable_prediction: after implementing the adaptive signal timing system, average intersection delay will decrease by 15% during non-incident conditions, and the system will recover to within 5% of optimal delay within 10 minutes of an incident, compared to the current centrally-optimized system
